papers.title: Reinforcement Learning in Machine Learning
papers.summary: Reinforcement Learning (RL) is a machine-learning approach for problems in which decisions are made repeatedly and their quality becomes clear through feedback. Instead of depending on a fixed collection of labelled answers, an RL agent interacts with an environment, observes its changing state, receives rewards or penalties, and improves its decision policy through experience. This review examines the basic RL framework and discusses deep reinforcement learning, offline learning, multi-agent systems, and human-guided learning. papers.title: Environmental Perception and Intelligent Navigation for Autonomous Delivery Robots in Complex Scenarios
papers.summary: Autonomous delivery robots (ADRs) face perception and navigation challenges in complex scenarios. When operating in real world urban environments, ADRs have trouble negotiating upturned streets, uneven terrain, and moving obstacles. This review covers three key areas: environmental perception, navigation techniques, and mechanical adaptability of delivery vehicles. papers.summary: As humanoid robots are increasingly used in complex real-world environments, reliable verification of robot actions becomes more important. Action verification should not only check whether the executed action matches the intended instruction, but also keep reliable performance when motor-sensor observations are affected by failures. Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning for Coordinated Emergency Building Sweeps
papers.summary: We develop a Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) framework for coordinating emergency responders during building sweeps. The problem is formulated as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP) that captures building topology, occupant vulnerability, dynamic hazards, and partial observability. In the six-room office baseline, MADDPG reaches a 134-second sweep time after 5,000 episodes, within 6.3% of the 126-second theoretical optimum and outperforming PPO and DQN. papers.summary: Upper-limb amputation seriously affects a person's daily life. papers.summary: Many artificial intelligence programs require powerful computing hardware, whereas agricultural robots, drones, and smart cameras rely on small embedded devices with limited computing power, battery capacity, and heat dissipation. Lightweight models reduce parameters and computational costs while maintaining acceptable accuracy, enabling AI deployment on resource-constraint network devices. papers.title: Multi-Robot Collaborative SLAM in Warehouses: A Review
papers.summary: With the rapid growth of e-commerce, Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) are increasingly deployed in intelligent warehouses, where Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) provides the core localization capability. Warehouses differ from domestic or outdoor scenarios in four respects: highly structured regular rack layouts, quasi-static conditions with dynamic goods movement, GPS-denied weak-network communication, and perceptual degradation caused by long corridors and repetitive textures. This paper reviews recent progress in multi-robot collaborative SLAM tailored for warehouse scenarios.
